title: ChatRequest
description: The body the browser POSTs to /api/chat. It carries the whole tree every time; the service is stateless.

tree.description: The tree as the browser currently holds it.

company.description: The org the tree hangs off, if the browser has one: the teams nodes reference by unitId, with their charters.

selectedNodeId.description: Id of the node the user has selected, or null. "this" and "it" in the message refer to it.

history.description: Earlier turns of the conversation, oldest first.

context.description: What the user has on screen as they type. Advisory: it is how "this", "those" and "the team" resolve without the user naming anything.

mode.description: What kind of conversation this tab is. Absent means "free".

subject.description: The one thing an interview tab is about. Absent or null in a free conversation.

chatMode.title: ChatMode
chatMode.description: How this conversation is being held. "free" is the default coach conversation: the user asks, you answer. The three interview modes invert that — you ask, one question per turn, and end by proposing actions. "audit": no user question and no conversation at all; read the whole tree and return `findings`. "persona": you are not the coach at all — you speak as one team, out of its charter, and say "we".

chatSubject.title: ChatSubject
chatSubject.description: The one thing this conversation is about: an existing node, a team (the subject of an interview, or the team a persona conversation speaks as), or the parent a new node will hang under. Null in a free conversation, which is about the whole tree, and in an audit.

oneOf.description: One existing node in the tree.
A node that does not exist yet, and where it will go.
No subject: the conversation is about the whole document.

nodeSubject.title: NodeSubject
nodeSubject.description: An interview about one existing node.

id.description: Id of the node the interview is about.

teamSubject.title: TeamSubject
teamSubject.description: One team: the subject of a charter interview, or the team a persona conversation speaks as.

id.description: Id of the team in company.units the interview is about.

newNodeSubject.title: NewNodeSubject
newNodeSubject.description: An interview that ends by adding a node the tree does not have yet.

parentId.description: Id of the node the new one will hang under, or null when the user has not decided yet — in which case the first question is which objective it supports.

viewContext.title: ViewContext
viewContext.description: The user's view at the moment they pressed send: which panel is open, what is pulsing in the 3D scene, which document they are in. Everything here is optional and advisory — the service drops anything that names something the tree or the org does not have.

panel.description: The side panel over the 3D scene, or null when none is open. Only one panel is ever open at a time.

anyOf.description: The panel the user has open.
No panel is open; the user is looking at the bare scene.

highlighted.description: Ids of the nodes pulsing in the scene right now — the ones you highlighted in your last reply, unless the user has since selected something. "those", "them" and "these" refer to this set.

dataset.description: Title of the document the user is looking at, so you can name it the way they see it in the picker.

openPanel.title: OpenPanel
openPanel.description: The panel open over the 3D scene: one node's detail, one team's charter, the list of teams, or the briefing of what the last audit found.

kind.description: What the panel is showing: "node" one OKR node, "team" one team's charter, "teams" the list of all teams, "briefing" the findings from the last audit.

id.description: The node id when kind is "node", the team id when kind is "team". Absent for the teams list.

editing.description: True when the node panel is in edit mode, so the user is changing the node rather than reading it. Team panels are always editable and omit this.

field.description: The field the user's cursor is in right now, if any. "this" in a message like "what should this be?" means that field of this node or team.
